messages:
ana: Quick Q — noticed a lot of node churn in staging after I applied a terraform change to enable the Karpenter provisioner but left cluster-autoscaler enabled. Pods behind HPAs sometimes don't scale even though HPA shows high utilization. Anyone seen this combo cause churn or weird HPA behavior?

ben: Short answer: yes. CA + Karpenter can fight each other. CA expects long-lived ASG nodes; Karpenter creates short-lived nodes on demand. If both try to manage capacity you can get flapping. :eyes:

carl: Quick checklist I run: 
- `kubectl get hpa -A` 
- `kubectl describe hpa -n staging <name>` 
- `kubectl get vpa -A` 
- `kubectl describe provisioner karpenter-provisioner -n karpenter` 
- `kubectl logs -n karpenter deploy/karpenter --tail=200`
These usually show if HPAs are being starved by node provisioning or if VPA changed requests.

maya: Also, VPA in `Auto` mode will update pod requests which changes the HPA's denominator (requested CPU). That can easily produce oscillation: VPA lowers requests -> HPA sees higher % -> scales -> Karpenter makes nodes -> CA may later scale down ASGs -> churn. For HPA + VPA, recommended is `updateMode: Off` for workloads using HPA.

ana: typo — (ana) I did have a VPA on `ingestion-svc` set to `Auto`. HPA target is 60% CPU and requests were small. So VPA lowering requests could be amplifying HPA.

ben: Exactly. More specifics: HPA (CPU) computes: `(current CPU usage / requested CPU) * 100`. If VPA reduces requests, the percentage spikes even if absolute CPU is modest, causing scale-ups. If CA removes its ASG nodes while Karpenter provisions and they have different scale-down windows, you end up with node churn.

carl: If you're migrating to Karpenter, pick one autoscaler. Steps I recommend: 
1) In terraform, set `module.cluster_autoscaler.enabled = false` (or remove the helm_release).
2) Remove or decommission ASGs that CA was managing so there isn't an orphaned autoscaler.
3) Ensure Karpenter Provisioner has sane ttl and consolidation settings so it doesn't immediately zap nodes.

carl: Example terraform change (very small diff):
```hcl
module "cluster_autoscaler" {
  source  = "git::ssh://.../modules/cluster-autoscaler.git"
  enabled = false
}

module "karpenter" {
  source  = "git::ssh://.../modules/karpenter.git"
  enabled = true
}
```

maya: Karpenter provisioner snippet for reference (yaml):
```yaml
apiVersion: karpenter.sh/v1alpha5
kind: Provisioner
metadata:
  name: default
spec:
  ttlSecondsAfterEmpty: 300
  consolidation:
    enabled: true
  requirements:
  - key: node.kubernetes.io/instance-type
    operator: In
    values: [m6i.large, m6i.xlarge]
  provider:
    subnetSelector:
      karpenter.sh/discovery: my-cluster
    securityGroupSelector:
      kubernetes.io/cluster/my-cluster: "owned"
```

maya: Also make sure IRSA is wired for the karpenter controller. Example TF for the service account IAM role: 
```hcl
resource "aws_iam_role" "karpenter_controller" {
  name = "karpenter-controller-role"
  # assume role policy for OIDC
}

resource "kubernetes_service_account" "karpenter" {
  metadata {
    name      = "karpenter"
    namespace = "karpenter"
    annotations = {
      "eks.amazonaws.com/role-arn" = aws_iam_role.karpenter_controller.arn
    }
  }
}
```

ben: Troubleshooting commands to run if you see no scaling: 
- `kubectl describe hpa -n <ns> <hpa-name>` -> check current/target & events
- `kubectl describe pod -n <ns> <pod>` -> check requests/limits after VPA edits
- `kubectl get nodes -o wide` -> spot different node types/labels
- `kubectl get prov -n karpenter -o yaml` -> see last provision attempts
- `kubectl logs -n karpenter deploy/karpenter | grep -i failed`

carl: Extra gotcha: make sure your HPA metrics source is healthy (metrics-server or custom metrics). If metrics are stale HPA will not scale. `kubectl top pod -n <ns>` should return numbers.

deploy-bot: Terraform plan applied in staging: removed `helm_release.cluster-autoscaler` and applied `module.karpenter.enabled = true`. Watch staging for 30m.

ana: (ana) Thanks — I'll open two PRs: one to flip `ingestion-svc` VPA `updateMode` to `Off`, and one to disable cluster-autoscaler in terraform (and add a note in the migration doc). I'll ping for review. :thumbsup:

ben: PR checklist for this migration (copy to your PR body):
- [ ] terraform plan shows `cluster_autoscaler` removal (no new ASGs)
- [ ] karpenter provisioner `ttlSecondsAfterEmpty` >= 300 and `consolidation` enabled
- [ ] VPA updateMode set to `Off` for HPA'd workloads
- [ ] metrics-server healthy (`kubectl top pods` returns values)
- [ ] smoke canary deployed (reduce replica counts then ramp) and monitor karpenter/controller logs
- [ ] monitor cloudwatch/cost for unexpected scale-ups in first 1hr

carl: If anyone hits `Failed to provision` in karpenter logs after CA removal, paste the log. Usually it's IAM or subnet selectors mismatch.

ana: Will do. Thanks everyone.

maya: TL;DR: don't run CA + Karpenter together; set VPA to Off for HPA workloads; check metrics-server and karpenter IRSA. :white_check_mark:
